_meta.indication: Limited population indication, as part of a combination regimen with bedaquiline and linezolid, for the treatment of adults with pulmonary extensively drug resistant (XDR), treatment-intolerant or nonresponsive multidrug-resistant (MDR) tuberculosis (TB).

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label, noncomparative trial with efficacy assessed against historical controls; conducted at three sites in South Africa
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with pulmonary XDR-TB or treatment-intolerant/nonresponsive MDR-TB (TI/NR MDR-TB)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Treatment failure, defined as bacteriologic failure, bacteriologic relapse, or clinical failure through follow-up until 6 months after the end of treatment (favorable outcome = absence of treatment failure)
pivotal_trials.n: 109 patients treated; primary analysis of 45 patients agreed with the Agency
pivotal_trials.result: Favorable outcome in 40/45 (89%, 95% CI 76%-96%) in the agreed-to primary population; 95/107 (89%, 95% CI 81%-94%) at the January 18, 2019 cutoff. BPaL success far exceeded the prespecified 50% historical control threshold; vs matched historical control 11%, Relative Risk 64.5, 95% CI [9 to 472], p < 0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) include peripheral neuropathy, acne, anemia, nausea, and vomiting. In Study 1 (N=109), peripheral neuropathy occurred in 88 (81%), acne 42 (39%), anemia 40 (37%), nausea 40 (37%), and vomiting 37 (34%). Serious findings included hepatotoxicity, myelosuppression, optic/peripheral neuropathy, QT prolongation, and lactic acidosis. Eight (7.3%) of 109 subjects died.
target_moa: Pretomanid is a nitroimidazooxazine antimycobacterial drug. It kills actively replicating M. tuberculosis by inhibiting mycolic acid biosynthesis (blocking cell wall production); under anaerobic conditions, bioreduction (via a deazaflavin F420-dependent nitroreductase) generates reactive nitrogen species causing respiratory poisoning of M. tuberculosis.

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory Committee meeting held June 6, 2019; voted 14 Yes, 4 No that the applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness and sufficient evidence of safety.

description.text: Modified linezolid dosage regimen (Preferred and Alternative) and added an alternative bedaquiline dosage regimen in the BPaL combination based on ZeNix Trial data

summary.text: Pretomanid was approved August 14, 2019 under the Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD, section 506(h)), as part of the BPaL regimen. It held orphan-drug and Fast Track designations (both 2007) and QIDP designation (2017), and received priority review (via GAIN section 524A and independently). The sponsor also received a tropical disease priority review voucher.

citations.quote: As the benefit-risk considerations of pretomanid in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid only support its use in a limited population of patients with pulmonary XDR-TB or TI/NR MDR-TB, the NDA is being approved under the Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD).
